articles.title: Amazon boosts same-day delivery to take on Instacart, Walmart
articles.content: STORY: Amazon announced on Wednesday that it is expanding its grocery fast-delivery option for its Prime members to include perishable items like fruit, milk and frozen dinners.It's the latest move by Amazon to compete with grocery delivery services offered by Walmart and Instacart.Amazon’s stock rose as much as 1.5 percent in Wednesday morning trading while Walmart slipped as much as 2 and a half percent and Instacart plunged 12% at one point.Amazon shoppers in more than 1,000 U.S. cities, including Phoenix and Tampa, can already get doorstep delivery within hours of placing an order.Amazon plans to expand its fast-delivery service to 2,300 cities by the end of the year.The company announced in June it is investing $4 billion to bring same-day and next-day delivery services to more than 4,000 rural U.S. communities by the end of the year as well.Previously, Prime subscribers' grocery orders were fulfilled through Amazon Fresh or Whole Foods. Now the additional service will complete orders through its same-day delivery logistics locations.Prime members who pay about $15 a month or $149 a year will get this benefit for free for orders over $25 which is the minimum required for free delivery for Walmart+ members who pay $98 a year. Walmart said in May that it will soon be able to offer delivery within three hours to 95% of the U.S. population, and that faster delivery speeds are helping drive its business. Between February and April, Walmart reported a 91% increase in deliveries under three hours compared with the same period last year.One analyst told Reuters the move by Amazon to lower the minimum order to $25 directly threatens Instacart by enabling customers to use Amazon for quick, one-off purchases, which is a core part of Instacart's main appeal.
